result.title: TESS: Query-Guided Temporal Event-Structured Frame Selection for Long-Video Understanding
result.summary: Temporal localization in long videos is challenging because brief, question-relevant events are dispersed among extensive redundant content. Limited visual budgets increase the risk of omitting these events or their temporal context, undermining reliable reasoning. Existing frame selection methods emphasize semantic relevance or temporal coverage, often overlooking the complementary evidence needed to locate related events and establish their temporal relationships. To address this limitation, we propose TESS, a training-free framework for query-guided temporal event-structured frame selection. TESS selects frames that jointly show the reference event and the event asked about, in the required temporal order. Leveraging frozen vision-language representations, TESS integrates soft temporal gating, role-aware budget allocation, and within-role redundancy suppression to preserve complementary event evidence. Extensive experiments across four long-video understanding benchmarks and three multimodal backbones demonstrate that TESS consistently outperforms the strongest compared baseline by 4.0-5.5 percentage points under a fixed frame budget. Further analyses reveal greater improvements on longer videos and robust performance under tighter visual budgets, while independent evidence annotations confirm enhanced event and temporal-relation coverage. These findings establish explicit temporal evidence organization as an effective training-free strategy for preserving event relationships and supporting efficient temporal reasoning over long videos. Our code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/TESS_code.

AI.brief_summary: 提出免训练的 TESS 长视频帧选择框架：以查询引导同时选出参考事件与目标事件的帧并保持时序顺序，结合软时序门控、角色感知预算分配与同角色冗余抑制，在固定帧预算下保留互补事件证据。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接对应 LVR 中「LOOK」阶段的视觉证据筛选与预算成本问题，其角色化预算分配和冗余抑制可供核查：固定视觉预算下证据互补性如何影响时序关系推理，以及选择信号是否真正被下游答案使用。
